original.target_description: Original US study: two-tailed bivariate correlation between self-reported political orientation (−5 liberal to +5 conservative) and ERN amplitude in the Go/No-Go task; 43 right-handed participants.

n.location: PDF p. 1, participant description; p. 2, correlation results
n.quote: we recorded electroencephalographs from 43 right-handed subjects (63% female)
n.sample_role: Participants in the target bivariate correlation; printed recruitment N is supported by target r(41) degrees of freedom.
n.exclusions: No participant exclusion is documented in the two-page main article; target correlation degrees of freedom are consistent with all 43 participants.

es.quote: Political orientation was strongly correlated with ERN amplitudes (r(41) ¼ 0.59, P o 0.001; Fig. 1a), as well as with No-Go N2 amplitudes (r(41) ¼ 0.41, P o 0.01).

p.quote: Political orientation was strongly correlated with ERN amplitudes (r(41) ¼ 0.59, P o 0.001; Fig. 1a), as well as with No-Go N2 amplitudes (r(41) ¼ 0.41, P o 0.01).

replication.target_description: Czech university-student replication, ages 20–26: Spearman rank correlation of self-evaluated liberalism/conservatism and ERN amplitude; retained electrophysiological sample of 95. Self-evaluation rather than separately validated political orientation matches the original target.

n.quote: This requirement shrunk our group by five participants to 95 persons.
n.sample_role: Participants retained for electrophysiological analyses and the target correlation.
n.exclusions: Five of 100 participants excluded by the minimum of six epochs requirement for ERN estimation; Figure 2 reports 95 participants for both ERN and N2 responses.

reported_success.quote: Contrary to the original Am2007 study, we found no relationship between the ERN or N2 NoGo and L/C orientation based on the self-evaluation in the larger homogenous cohort of 100 participants.

notes: Titles verified in both retrieved full PDFs. Text is a frozen pdftotext -layout parse; original PDF uses ¼ for = and o for <. Original target is the unadjusted bivariate correlation, not the partial ERN correlation controlling behavioral accuracy. Replication discussion refers to the recruited cohort of 100; analytic electrophysiological sample is 95 as documented by footnote 2 and Figure 2. Authors describe a test in a different sociocultural context. No metrics were converted.
